# An exact all-facet loss in an unrestricted self-coupling repair

This is a probe of a stronger auxiliary claim, not of OC or an actual
stationary H configuration. The general diagonal self-coupling
obstruction is already archived in Registry138 and
actual-surface-entropy-pays-discounted-parity-repair-rate-geometry.md.
The construction below adds an exact all-facet simplex cap-load loss
with compatible positive actual fibers and a homothetic plateau.
It does not reopen the self-coupling route without new prescribed
distinct marginals or other actual pairing constraints.

## 1. Actual bodies and all canonical simplex caps

Let d>=2 and let D be a centered d-simplex with vertices v_0,...,v_d
and affine barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d.
Put t=1/(d+1), choose 0<delta<t, and select distinct i,j.
Let

    K_A=(1-delta)v_i+delta D,
    K_B=(1-delta)v_j+delta D,
    K_M=(K_A+K_B)/2.

For the canonical caps H_l={lambda_l>=t}, every point of K_A lies
in exactly H_i, every point of K_B lies in exactly H_j, and every
point of K_M lies in exactly H_i and H_j. Indeed the endpoint
distinguished coordinate is at least 1-delta, the other coordinates
are at most delta, and both distinguished midpoint coordinates are
at least (1-delta)/2>t.

Realize these at integer bases A=(0,0), M=(1,0), B=(2,0).
Take C to be the convex hull of those two endpoint fibers and the
product [0,2] times [1,3] times D. More precisely the first two
coordinates are the base coordinates and the last d are continuous.
Then the base projection is [0,2] times [0,3], all sampled fibers
are positive, and at second base coordinate zero the actual fibers
are the Minkowski interpolation of K_A and K_B. At every base in
[0,2] times [1,3] the actual fiber is D. Thus C is canonical,
ambient full-dimensional and contained in the common constant
homothetic envelope D. Its plateau has the relative-interior integer
witness (1,2). No deepestness or actual common-Q claim is made.

Let eta be the actual boundary-area measure on the normal bundle of
all sampled fibers. Let mu_A, mu_B, mu_M be its restrictions to the
three bottom-row fibers. These are translates of one common
delta-scaled simplex surface measure. Write their common total mass
as s>0 and put gamma=mu_A+mu_B.

## 2. A capped repair loses exactly one quarter of the old cap load

The translation swapping K_A and K_B gives a normal-preserving
self-coupling of gamma whose midpoint law is

    rho_0=2 mu_M.

All d+1 facet normals are included. Give the canonical caps any
positive weights omega_l summing to one, and write
W=sum_l omega_l 1_(H_l). Its rho_0 integral is

    integral W d rho_0=2s(omega_i+omega_j).             (1)

Consider ANY coupling with both marginals gamma and midpoint law
rho<=eta. Its only possible output bases are A,M,B. The two cross
base flows have equal mass r by marginal balance. Thus the midpoint
mass is 2r at M and s-r at each endpoint. Since eta at M has mass s,
one has r<=s/2. The cap values just proved are constant on all
possible midpoint supports, so

    integral W d rho=(omega_i+omega_j)(s+r)
       <=(3/2)s(omega_i+omega_j)
       =(3/4) integral W d rho_0.                     (2)

The estimate holds in particular for normal-preserving repairs; it
does not rely on dropping any facet normal.

It is sharp, including convex-order improvement. Mix the diagonal
self-coupling and the translated swap in equal proportions. Its
midpoint law is

    rho=(1/2)mu_A+mu_M+(1/2)mu_B<=eta.

Jensen under the common translation identifies
2mu_M<=_cx mu_A+mu_B, hence rho_0<=_cx rho.
This law has r=s/2 and attains equality in (2).

## 3. Why hinge maximization does not preserve this cross pairing

For the selected hinge phi_i=(lambda_i-t)_+, compare a pair with the
same underlying xi in D:

    x_A=(1-delta)v_i+delta xi,
    x_B=(1-delta)v_j+delta xi.

The diagonal-minus-cross midpoint hinge total is

    phi_i(x_A)+phi_i(x_B)-2phi_i((x_A+x_B)/2)
       =t-delta lambda_i(xi)>0.

The analogous formula holds for j. Thus any positive combination
of the selected i and j hinges strictly prefers the diagonal law.
More generally every self-coupling has midpoint law below gamma
in convex order by Jensen, and the diagonal coupling attains gamma.
Any constraint of the form nu_source<=_cx rho is preserved on
replacing rho by gamma. A strictly convex objective forces the
diagonal almost surely.

This last fact is the already archived obstruction. The new example
quantifies the cap loss and verifies it on all actual simplex facet
normals. It does not refute a global 2^n ceiling, a coupling with
prescribed distinct endpoint marginals, or a marked constraint which
specifies more than the source law and its conditional barycenter.
